objective: Confirmatory Monte Carlo of the four twist sectors on common random numbers: rectangle additivity at aspects 1, 3/2, 2 and 3 with two-size extrapolation; additivity in the orthogonal basis on the 45-degree rotated square, and its failure in the axis basis; odd-winding additivity and the consistency relation on rectangles; the harmonic content of E and O under shear on squares and on the 2:1 torus, reported.
status: Closed: refuted by TWIST-RELATIONS-20261022-001B-E001 (confirmatory Monte Carlo, frozen contract, 32 rows, 1710 s). Controls pass: the strong-component and odd-cluster tests agree on every sample; contractible and cross counts agree in every twisted sector; inconsistency equals cross plus odd windings exactly. The independent checker matches the 3 x 3 rows to the exact fractions of TWIST-RELATIONS-20261022-001A-P001 and replays 7 x 5 by other code. Primary candidates. The odd-line identity is accepted: for each class, the two twists odd on it give the same probability that the cone is that line; 24 tests on 8 new tori, max |z| 2.63, resolved to about 1e-5. The stronger form, a shear-independent odd horizontal line, is decisively rejected: on 12 x 8 the probability is 0.000918, 0.000913, 0.000866, 0.000861 at shears 0, 2, 4, 6 (z = -0.65, -6.65, -7.31). Its exact equality on 3 x 3, 4 x 3 and 3 x 4 was a small-torus coincidence. Secondary, both accepted: rectangle additivity at aspects 3/2, 2, 3 (D_inf = 0.0025 +- 0.0014, 0.0004 +- 0.0012, 0.0005 +- 0.0010); the orthogonal-basis relation on the 45-degree rotated square, at 2.5 sigma (0.0043 +- 0.0017, not yet decaying; the axis basis gives -0.27). Reported: on 64 x 64 squares the vertical-twist effect is shear-independent (-0.134 +- 0.001) and the horizontal-twist effect is a single first harmonic, so D(s) = D(0) + E(0)(1 - cos(pi s/64)) to 0.001; on the 2:1 torus higher harmonics appear.
title: Experiment: the twist relations across shapes
